subject: GPU corridor + warm-start options for GlacierBio — sizing and ramp
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@glacierbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GPU corridor + warm-start options for GlacierBio — sizing and ramp

Alex —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our discussion, attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options that map expected production traffic curves into concrete cluster sizes, minimums, and a practical ramp cadence. High level: we recommend a corridor-based approach (Option A/B/C) so GlacierBio can preserve a cost floor while giving headroom for burst and model experimentation.

Summary (attached: GlacierBio_Dedicated_Options_Q4.pdf):
- Option A — Staging corridor (recommended): 16 min GPUs / 40 burstable GPUs; 3-month warm-start; canary at 8 GPUs for first 30 days; target 99th pct p99 tokens latency guardrails; monthly decaying credits for warm-start training work.
- Option B — Growth corridor: 32 min GPUs / 64 burstable GPUs; 2-month warm-start; includes 48-hour capacity burst windows for steady-state traffic spikes.
- Option C — Heavy reserve (compressed SLO): 64 min GPUs / 96 burstable GPUs; aggressive discounting but higher committed spend.

Ramp & activation notes (we can tailor):
- Pilot (optional): 4–8 GPUs for 4–6 weeks to validate inference pipelines and KV cache warm-up.
- Month 0–1: canary (8 GPUs) + prefetching cadence to populate KV caches.
- Month 2–4: staged activation to min quota, monitor token-level cost; we recommend a 15% warm buffer above forecasted baseline.

Pricing callouts (indicative): per-GPU-hour blended for committed lanes, burst at market rate; warm-start crediting schedule included in the PDF.

Next steps: if you like one of the options I’ll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones (pilot -> contract signature -> production ramp). Happy to drop in our SRE lead for a short call about warm-start mechanics.

Attachments: GlacierBio_Dedicated_Options_Q4.pdf (proposal summary)

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

---

From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@glacierbio.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@glacierbio.com>, Procurement <procurement@glacierbio.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU corridor + warm-start options for GlacierBio — sizing and ramp

Sean —

Thanks for the thoughtful options and the PDF. A few quick Qs from our side before we pull procurement in: 

1) For Option A (staging corridor) can you unpack what you mean by "warm-start credits" and how they apply to our training runs? Are those credits applied against committed spend or separate line items?

2) We want to understand the min GPUs guarantee — specifically: if we commit to 16 min GPUs, what happens in scenarios where utilization is consistently below 12 GPUs for 2+ months? Any pause/stepdown language?

3) Pilot timing — we'd prefer a short pilot (4 weeks) but need a clear acceptance checklist (latency, error-rate, embedding freshness). Can you add that to the MAP?

Procurement is copied to start thinking about contract lead times. If you can sketch a draft MAP (milestones + owners + signoffs) we’ll review internally.

Appreciate it —
Alex Grant
Head of AI Platform | GlacierBio
alex.grant@glacierbio.com

Subject: Re: GPU corridor + warm-start options for GlacierBio — sizing and ramp (internal)

Quick internal note — think through a slightly more conservative stepdown and a single predictable cadence for warm-start credits. Proposed edits to Option A: 

- Pilot: 4 weeks at 8 GPUs with explicit acceptance (latency < 120ms p95, error-rate < 0.5%, embedding freshness defined as < 2hr lag for new records).
- Activation cadence: 8 -> 16 (min) over 6 weeks; allow a one-time stepdown to 12 GPUs if sustained utilization < 60% over a full calendar month, with a 30-day notice and a 2% stepdown fee.
- Canary & rollback: include a canary at 8 GPUs for 14 days post-contract-signature to validate KV cache behavior; automatic rollback policy if token-loss > 1% or p95 exceeds SLA by > 30%.

I attached a quick worksheet with the activation weeks and burn estimate, helps us model cash flows.

Attachment: Ramp_Cadence_worksheet.xlsx

LMK if you want me to bake these edits into the updated PDF for client send.

-Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@glacierbio.com>, Procurement <procurement@glacierbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU corridor + warm-start options for GlacierBio — sizing and ramp

Alex / Procurement —

Appended an updated Option A that incorporates Karthik's stepdown language and a short acceptance checklist for the pilot. Key clarifications: 

- Warm-start credits: these are credit dollars applied against the committed monthly invoice, allocated to non-production training/weight warm-up runs. Credits vest over the 3-month warm-start period (month 1 = 60%, month 2 = 30%, month 3 = 10%) and cannot be used for third-party storage.
- Stepdown: one-time permitted stepdown to 12 GPUs after 30 days notice if utilization below 60% for a full calendar month; a 2% contractual fee on the monthly committed spend for administrative re-provisioning.
- Pilot acceptance: p95 latency < 120ms, error-rate < 0.5%, KV cache hit-rate > 70% for typical workflows.

I attached the updated client-facing PDF (GlacierBio_Final_Option_A.pdf) and included a short MAP link below. If Procurement confirms lead times we can lock dates — suggested signature target 2026-12-10 to align with Q1 runway.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/GLC-2026-042 

Attachments: GlacierBio_Final_Option_A.pdf

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Sean / team —

Appreciate the quick turn. Option A (the staging corridor) looks like the best fit for our org given the uncertainty in model rollout velocity. Two quick items before we move to formal procurement: 

1) Can you add language that the warm-start credits are auditable (we need a usage report that shows how credits were applied)?
2) Procurement asks for a sample SOW paragraph describing responsibilities for KV cache pre-warm tasks (who runs prefetch vs. what Redwood will do).

If you can add those two items to the final MAP/contract attachment I’ll route to Procurement. We are comfortable with the suggested signature target of 2026-12-10.

Thanks — excited to get started.

Alex Grant
